name: Photo relief wall
description:
Background-free grayscale photo relief on a wall 12 studs wide, 8 bricks high, and 2 studs deep. Body 95.8 x 15.8 x 76.8 mm, or 78.6 mm including top studs. Twenty-eight separate interlocking bricks (twenty 2 x 4 and eight 2 x 2) in alternating rows of 4+4+4 and 2+4+4+2 studs. Plain, unnumbered backs.
The supplied portrait was prepared as a grayscale cutout. Darker tones are recessed and lighter tones raised: approximately 0.45 mm below to 0.9 mm above the front plane. Transparent background remains flat. This is a grayscale-driven relief, not reconstructed anatomical depth. Maximum recess leaves at least 1.05 mm of the original 1.5 mm front wall. Uses the tested 5.0 mm studs and original underside geometry.
Print photo-relief-wall.stl once for all 28 bricks; combined.stl is preview-only. Split the plate into objects in your slicer to extract individual bricks. Print at 100% scale, studs up, open undersides on the bed, supports and internal brims off, starting with 0.12 mm layers. Matte light-colored filament and light from the side will make the shallow relief easier to see. Inspect the sliced raised features before printing.
Assemble rows from bottom to top; the print plate keeps each course in its own row with the bottom course at the back (+Y), top at the front (-Y), and parts ordered left to right (+X). Preserve the portrait orientation shown in the preview. Do not scale the STL to make a smaller wall, as that also changes stud fit; regenerate the brick layout instead. Photo-relief detail and print quality still need a physical test.
